hypotheses.justification: If S = ∅, both sides equal [] for every k. Simplified.Candidate M F ∅ p k q requires q.toFinset ⊆ ∅ (so q = []) and p.length < q.length = 0, which is impossible. So no candidate exists, the `dite` in sampleRun takes the else branch, and sampleRun naturalCheckpoints F ∅ k = [] by induction. Likewise testCandidate F ∅ p k q contains the same two conjuncts (q.toFinset ⊆ S, p.length < q.length), so candidateCodes F ∅ p k = ∅, and pickWord ∅ = [] by its else branch; hence executableRun F ∅ k = [] by induction. Proof without hS: split on S.Nonempty (as executableNormalized_eq in the same file already does). In the nonempty case use the existing proof. In the empty case, rewrite S = ∅ via Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty and prove executableRun F ∅ k = [] ∧ sampleRun naturalCheckpoints F ∅ k = [] by induction on k, using the two emptiness facts above. (hF is genuinely needed: without freshness there can be a step where no candidate exists, so sampleRun keeps a nonempty history while executableRun returns pickWord ∅ = [].)
